#1992. Hearts unbeaten home record obliterated as swashbuckling Falkirk earn 31-year first

Rampant Falkirk obliterated Hearts’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle as they leapfrogged the Jambos into third place.

Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury amid a gruelling fixture list, were in disarray as the swashbuckling Bairns romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hearts hit back through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025. To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos, who have won just two of their last 11 matches, lost yet another senior player as Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

There were two changes to the Hearts side that started Thursday’s Conference League defeat to Thun as Stephen Kingsley and Guendouz were replaced by Yan Dhanda and Landry Kabore.

Falkirk boss John McGlynn, named manager of the month for October, made one enforced change from the side that defeated Celtic last Sunday as Jack McMillan took over from injured right-back Ryan Strain.

The Bairns seized the lead in the fourth minute. After Murrell’s close-range effort from Scott Tanser’s cross was brilliantly saved by Beau Reus, Barbrook reacted quickest to drill home a low, angled finish from eight yards out.

Hearts threatened an equaliser in the 10th minute, but Kabore’s effort on the turn from the edge of the six-yard box was superbly blocked by Scott Bain.

Falkirk doubled their lead in the 17th minute after the hosts were caught wide open on the counter-attack. Dhanda’s shot from distance was charged down, allowing the Bairns to break swiftly, with Brad Spencer weighting his pass perfectly for Eames, who fired past the exposed Reus.

Braga thought he had pulled one back for Hearts in the 20th minute, but it was ruled out for handball.

Falkirk took full advantage of this reprieve by adding a third in the 33rd minute as Murrell peeled off Fagan-Walcott at the back post to nod home Deniss Melniks’ cross from the right.

The visitors struck again in first-half stoppage-time as Henderson curled high past Reus after Tanser’s corner broke to him just inside the box.

As jeers rained down from an irate home support, Vrancken replaced midfielders Laurent Mendy and Dhanda with Guendouz and Matthew Gillies for the start of the second half.

But within two minutes of the restart Falkirk notched again as Murrell fired home after being set up by Ethan Ross.

Hearts got off the mark when Guendouz drilled in his first goal for the club from just inside the box in the 50th minute.

Braga then tucked away a penalty in the 74th minute after Guendouz was tripped by Lewis Neilson, but it was not enough to prevent a third straight defeat for the Jambos.

#1991. MN24: Cardinale lines up attempt for Liverpool’s Van Dijk – the two conditions

Gerry Cardinale wants to make a statement centre-back signing and is targeting Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk, a report claims.

It is no secret that Milan want to sign a new central defender in January, but they will also be evaluating potential opportunities in view of next season too, to add some experience to what is quite a young department.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

According to MilanNews24, Cardinale has identified Van Dijk as a key signing to strengthen the defence. His contract with Liverpool – which expires in June – makes him a very tempting free transfer possibility, and he is the ‘big dream’ for next summer.

The Dutchman would represent a statement move for the Rossoneri, although the competition and financial demands make a potential deal anything but straightforward. Despite this, the Milan owner would like to make a concrete attempt, something La Gazzetta dello Sport also reported.

The RedBird Capital founder is willing to seriously evaluate the conditions for bringing the former Southampton and Celtic man to Italy. However, to even think about landing Van Dijk, there are two key conditions to be met.

The first is Champions League qualification, a crucial element in presenting the defender with an ambitious and competitive sporting project. The second is economic: a two-year contract worth €8-10m net per season would be needed.

It remains to be seen if Cardinale believes this is worth it, and what the incoming Head of Football Markus Krösche might think. However, Van Dijk would be a signing capable of bringing experience, leadership, quality and personality.

Town were without several key men so made a few adjustments to the team – but still lined up looking strong, showing the increasing competition for places.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The game sprang into life minutes before half-time as the busy Leo Ginger cut in from the left and let rip a stunning dipping strike from 25 yards that flew into the top right hand corner off the post.

What a great way to go into half-time… or so we thought. The visitors had other ideas as they hit back almost immediately breaking well at the other end of the pitch culminating in a fine finish into the top of the net by Abdulahi Abdulazeez.

The second period followed much of the pattern of the first, with the Barrowmen having the bulk of possession and playing some good football but lacking a bit of cutting edge.

The defining moment of the match came with 18 minutes to go as Charlie Pitcher broke down the right, taking a floating through ball superbly in his stride with a couple of great touches before sweeping home the winner in style. A great goal to win a less-than-great game.

Town saw out the remainder of the game with minimal fuss as they added three vital points to their league tally. The day was pretty much about grinding at a result when not at your best and overall it was really positive to do that when other games have got away from the team late on this season.

Steyning are 15th and next up – on Saturday – is a big test away to high-flying Hastings United.

#1989. Hearts crisis or just a bad week, is Vrancken in trouble and has Jamestown failed?

Welcome to The Burning Questions, our new daily debate where we take one major subject in Scottish sport and tackle the three questions everyone is talking about.

Each day, our writers will offer their verdicts on the biggest issues and arguments dominating the agenda. Hearts are generating plenty of debate currently, among their own supporters and rivals, after a miserable week for them despite a promising enough start to the season prior to that.

Defeat to archenemies Hibs in a Premier Sports Cup semi-final was bad enough, but they followed it up by losing 3-1 to FC Thun (ninth in the Swiss League) in the Conference League, and it could have been more that night. Yesterday, they were four goals down to Falkirk by half-time and lost 5-2 in the end. That certainly should not be happening at Tynecastle.

Fans are frustrated and some are already questioning the management of Wouter Vrancken after the Belgian's summer arrival. They are now also questioning the club's recruitment partner, Jamestown Analytics, after the failure of many of their summer signings to hit the ground running. Sporting director Graeme Jones is also in the firing line as a result of this.

They have been dealing with a ridiculous amount of injuries, particularly in defence and midfield, but many do not feel that is enough of a mitigating factor to excuse the form.

Matthew Lindsay and Blair Meikle give their answers to today’s three Burning Questions.

Some Hearts fans are starting to turn against Wouter Vrancken after recent results. Do you think that's fair or should he still have credit in the bank from earlier in the season?

Matthew Lindsay: As bad as the defeat to Falkirk at Tynecastle was yesterday, I think the Belgian is deserving of a little bit more understanding than he is currently receiving from a section of the Hearts support.

So many Scottish clubs have struggled to juggle European and domestic commitments over the years. With the number of injuries which the capital side have now, it is asking a lot of them to successfully negotiate their hectic schedule.

Did the mentally and physically draining encounter with Thun in Switzerland on Thursday night affect their performance this weekend? Few managers in the country would have been as grateful to get to the international break as Vrancken.

He has been a victim of his own success in some respects. His predecessors Robbie Neilson, Steven Naismith and Neil Critchley all struggled to fight on more than one front.

That said, after one win in eight, he desperately needs to get back to winning ways against Dundee away on Saturday, November 21.

Aberdeen 'set' to sack Stephen Robinson as axe looms at Pittodrie Robinson on the brink but Aberdeen’s deep-rooted problems go far beyond the manager

Blair Meikle: It is far, far too early to be turning on the head coach. Hearts currently sit fourth in the table and would jump back to third if they can win their game in hand - that is nowhere near a disaster or an endgame scenario. There were positive signs before all of the injuries and it is only around a month since fans were sharing clips and waxing lyrical about the football being played.

Despite all of that, there have been worrying signs in the last week in particular. Most notably the team being too vulnerable on the counter-attack, and conceding the same sort of goals over and over.

The Belgian did reference a lot of the missing players being ones who have "tactical awareness", so their return is something that could help with that.

However, Hearts have three very tough games after the international break (Dundee away, Monaco home, Celtic home) so another three negative results will really pile the pressure on.

The injuries decimating Hearts' squad have been well documented. To what extent can they be used as an excuse for the recent run, or should they be doing better even with the players available to them?

Matthew Lindsay: I think not having Craig Halkett, Harry Milne, Tom Renaud, Blair Spittal, Calvin Miller, Oisin McEntee, Christian Borchgrevink, Rogers Mato, Tomas Magnusson and Eduardo Ageu is a reasonable excuse for Hearts’ slump in form.

At the same time, I do think that Vrancken has to shoulder much of the responsibility for the displays. His tactics were naïve in the 7-1 defeat to Celtic at Parkhead. He could be given a pass for that debacle given that it was his first game in the East End of Glasgow. But shipping five to Falkirk at home is unforgivable.

Can his team produce the sort of fluid and expansive play that he favours when they are missing so many key men? He perhaps need to be a little bit more pragmatic in his current predicament.

Blair Meikle: The injuries cannot be ignored. I've heard a lot of people saying 'the injuries cannot be an excuse' - but of course they can, to an extent. Rob any manager of 11 members of his squad, mostly starters, and performances and results will take a hit.

For example, there is no way he wants to be playing Jamie McCart at left-back, and Stuart Findlay is someone he did not appear to fancy, yet they're making up half of his back four. They are two of the players who have cost him in recent games.

All that said, the team Hearts put out yesterday should not be conceding five goals at home, especially to a team that is not Celtic or Rangers, and the manager needs to take his share of the blame for that. And his decision to play Yan Dhanda in midfield was not one I agreed with.

I think confidence is a big issue just now and a big reason why players are doing things without conviction, both in and out of possession. But you need to be made of tougher stuff to play for Hearts.

Jamestown Analytics was seen as a gamechanger when the partnership was forged but there are questions around this summer's recruitment with signings like JJ Williams, Amadou Ba-Say and others not hitting the ground running. Does this, and the form under the new manager, raise doubts about the direction of the club under this model?

Matthew Lindsay: Jamestown Analytics may have been able to pluck players like Claudio Braga and Alexandros Kyziridis from relative obscurity, but the football intelligence consultancy has certainly had its failures.

It is fair to say that JJ Williams and Amadou Ba-Say have not proved value for money to date.

Many of the players who took Hearts to the brink of the Scottish title last season, not least Stuart Findlay and Oisin McEntee, were brought in on the recommendation of then manager Derek McInnes.

But a little patience is required. It took some time for the data-driven approach which Tony Bloom introduced at Brighton down in England and Royal Union Saint-Gilloise in Belgium to bear fruit. Mistakes were made along the way and invaluable lessons were learned.

Scottish football is a unique environment and it may be a few seasons before Jamestown tunes in fully to what is required for a player to meet its demands.

Blair Meikle: Like with the head coach question, it is too early to be writing off Jamestown Analytics. Especially when the evidence of how it has worked for Brighton, Union Saint-Gilloise, Como and others is there for all to see. Why would it all of a sudden flop here?

There are massive questions over much of the recruitment in the summer. Especially because neither Williams nor Ba-Sy have been what the club needed at centre-forward and the squad has been left massively short in defensive positions. A number of the summer arrivals do not look like being successes. However, it should be pointed out that Josh McPake, Calvin Miller, Beau Reus and Tom Renaud do, while Malachi Fagan-Walcott and Laurent Mendy have shown signs despite struggling in recent weeks.

It needs to be remembered that many of the early signings Union Saint-Gilloise made with Jamestown faded into obscurity, but the Belgian side made a few trades at modest profit before slowly building things up. Hearts have made a profit on Alexandros Kyziridis and Michael Steinwender, and Claudio Braga could still be the next on the conveyor belt. Then the JTA model can start to be ramped up.

#1988. This is an embarrassment – Wouter Vrancken rages after Hearts humiliation

Wouter Vrancken condemned a “ridiculous” first-half display from his sorry Hearts side as their 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership was ripped apart by ruthless Falkirk.

The beleaguered Jambos, who went into the game without 11 players through injury following a gruelling run of fixtures, endured a dismal afternoon as the Bairns raced into a 4-0 half-time lead on their way to a 5-2 victory at Tynecastle.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double had the visitors 5-0 up within 47 minutes before Hearts reduced the deficit through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle since April 2025 for the Jambos, who have now won just two of their last 11 matches in all competitions.

“This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure,” said Vrancken. “Always doubting, always doing things half-half, in possession, out of possession, everything, and such easy goals again.

“When you give those easy goals, then you cannot win a game. It’s childish goals and cannot happen on this level. Those simple things, they are the basics actually in these situations.

“It’s crazy, crazy, and everybody – me, staff, players – have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous.”

To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos lost yet another senior player as defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

“This also makes me a bit angry, because now we lose Mal again,” said Vrancken.

“Hopefully it’s not too bad, but still we had to replace him there, because he was one of the guys who were good in the game and in the last games actually he had a really consistent, good level.”

Hearts were leapfrogged into third place by Falkirk, who made it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time in 31 years.

“I’ve never been 5-0 up here before,” said Bairns manager John McGlynn. “First half we were outstanding. A great start to the game for us to get the goal so early.

“It was well documented about the Hearts injuries and, coming off the back of the game on Thursday night (in Thun), it was always going to be difficult for them.

“We had to smell blood and we had to go for it and that’s exactly what happened. The goals and our play were outstanding in the first half. We won every duel, we won everything all over the park.

“We got ourselves 4-0 up at half-time, which is dreamland. At 3pm, we never expected to be 4-0 up at half-time and certainly not 5-0 up a few minutes into the second half, which was another really good goal in transition.

“Hearts had a lot at the ball and dominated the second period, but we’re taking 5-2 every day of the week, make no mistake about it. It jumps us up into third place.

“Winning five on the trot has not been done since 1995, Jim Jefferies’ team, so I’m delighted for everyone at the football club that we’ve managed to equal that record.”

#1987. Hearts set for six-man injury boost as Wouter Vrancken bullish over revival

Wouter Vrancken is confident the impending return of no less than half a dozen key players from injury after the international break will help spark an upturn in fortunes for embattled Hearts.

The Jambos had 11 absentees for Sunday’s dismal 5-2 defeat at home to Falkirk and then lost key defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott in the second half.

Vrancken was optimistic that the centre-back had not sustained any serious damage and he is expecting his injury list to ease when his team return to action away to Dundee a week on Saturday.

The head coach reported that Eduardo Ageu, Tomas Magnusson, Rogers Mato, Blair Spittal, Oisin McEntee and Christian Borchgrevink are all in the frame to come back into contention, if not for Dens Park then certainly soon afterwards.

Read more: Hearts crisis or just a bad week, is Vrancken in trouble and has Jamestown failed?

“I think Eddie would be back, because he’s already training in the team,” said the head coach, offering an update on the injuries. “Tomas, for sure, because he has his protocol with the concussion.

“I think Spitts and Osh will be 50-50 when we come back. Mato, hopefully, if everything goes well.

“Christian is also maybe one who will be on the edge of coming back at this moment. I think these are the players (that are close).

“Stephen (Kingsley), we have to wait for the scan.”

Hearts have won just two of their last 11 matches amid a gruelling domestic and European schedule, leaving them fourth in the William Hill Premiership, out of the Premier Sports Cup and struggling to qualify for the Conference League knockout phase.

Vrancken is adamant that having a greater array of options available to select from will help them get back on track, however.

“I’m pretty confident in this, especially when we get numbers back, because these guys showed already what qualities and what extras they can bring on the pitch,” said the Belgian, whose side were on a nine-game unbeaten run before injuries started to undermine their campaign.

#1985. Why Kasper Hogh would not have taken Celtic penalty as Mika Baur injury addressed

Martin O’Neill admitted he would not have let Kasper Hogh take a second half penalty that Benjamin Nygren ended up failing to score in any case as Celtic squeezed past Kilmarnock at Parkhead.

The striker’s goal drought was extended to 16 games and he’s still to open his account at home for his new club. Defender Liam Scales was the match winner after converting a cross from Camilo Dusan in the 25th minute.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hogh had earlier endured the heartbreak of seeing a goal chalked off for a foul committed earlier in the move by Mika Baur and he snatched at a chance shortly afterwards when one-on-one with Kilmarnock ‘keeper Nico Mantl.

Hogh worked hard and was named man-of-the-match but was replaced after 70 minutes. Celtic were awarded a penalty shortly afterwards and many Celtic fans lamented Hogh not still being on the pitch to take it. However, O’Neill confirmed this wouldn’t have happened even if he had been available.

Nygren duly saw Mantl make an excellent save from his effort from 12 yards to keep Kilmarnock in the game. The visitors came close to equalising right at the death when Ieuan Owen failed to connect with a cross right in front of goal.

“We all thought Kasper had got off the mark,” said O’Neill, with reference to the goal that wasn’t. “We all thought that for about 35 seconds. I think myself that maybe he would have scored the next one had the first one counted but he worked exceptionally hard for us. I was pleased the team dug it out.

“We got the penalty but had he still been on the pitch I would not have asked him to take it. He might have missed. As it turned out, we did miss.

“In front of goal, it is proving a difficult one for him,” O'Neill added. “But he has worked exceptionally hard in the game, as he did on Thursday night (v Besiktas). I think things will come, honestly. He thought he had broken the spell but his hold up play was much, much better.”

Hogh received a warm ovation when he was replaced after 70 minutes by James Forrest. “I think that’s encouraging,” said O’Neill. “If you have the crowd behind you, if you’re working hard, they will forgive some other things. Now I am not saying that will last forever….Of course strikers live and die by their goals. But he feels we all believe in him in the dressing room, that’s encouraging for him.”

O’Neill stressed he had not seen a replay of the incident involving Baur that meant Hogh’s goal after 13 minutes was ruled off after a VAR check. Referee John Beaton was called to the monitor and he very abruptly signalled he was disallowing the strike.

“I have genuinely not seen it back because the little screen we have on the touchline is too small for me,” he said. “I can only go with what the lads were saying, they thought it was touch and go.”

O’Neill also revealed that Baur, who limped off near the end, had suffered ankle damage and has been booked in for a scan. The midfielder is due to join up with the Germany Under-21s in the international break.

“He’s in the treatment room,” he said. “His ankle is really sore and we don’t know the damage. We’ll wait until tomorrow to get a scan. Gosh, I’d hope he won’t be out terribly long but I don't know at the moment. He’s been great for us considering he’s not the tallest. He’d be about ten stone maybe not even that but his work rate is incredible. His overall reading of the game is really good and he’s not frightened.”

Ferencvaros striker Bamidele Yusuf is relishing the chance to play against AC Milan at an iconic stadium like San Siro.

For Milan, the task is quite a simple one tonight: they must beat their opponents from Hungary to get back on course in Europe and to keep alive their already slim hopes of getting into the top eight in the table, to get direct last-16 qualification.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, they are facing a team full of confidence that have not lost in their last 20 games across all competitions. Ferencvaros have also won three out of three in the Europa League too, beating Celtic, Viktoria Plzen and Torreense.

You have made many sacrifices to get to San Siro…

Did you analyse Milan’s derby win over Inter?

“They played an intense match against Inter, and we analysed the match in detail. However, we can’t draw conclusions based on how the derby unfolded. I’m curious to see how these ninety minutes unfold.”

However, Gross, 35, has played down talk of a title charge.

Diego Gomez put Brighton ahead after 15 minutes, sending a stunning left-footed strike from 25 yards into the top corner. The Paraguayan had scored from the halfway line against Crystal Palace on his previous appearance at the Amex.

Gross doubled Brighton’s lead shortly before half-time, firing his penalty into the top corner after Keane Lewis-Potter fouled Luka Vuskovic as they jostled at a set piece. Yasin Ayari forced a save from Caoimhin Kelleher before the interval.

Brighton controlled much of the second half as Brentford sat deep. The visitors finished without a shot on target and slipped to eighth, while Bart Verbruggen kept Brighton’s seventh clean sheet of the season, the most in the Premier League heading into the break.

#1982. Celtic pyschodrama engulfing team as VAR delivers mother of all smackdowns

Celtic built on their uplifting midweek victory over Besiktas but found the going hard against Neil McCann’s well-drilled team.

The champions possibly should have won by more than just Liam Scales’ 25th minute goal. However, Kasper Hogh’s woes are threatening to become a psychodrama afflicting the entire team.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Dane isn’t playing badly. Never mind the goal he scored after 13 minutes that was then very harshly chopped off for a foul in the build-up. Another shot midway through the second half appeared goal-bound until a heroic block from substitute MJ Kamson-Kamara deflected the ball over the bar. Events seem to be conspiring against him.

Hogh was subbed off with 20 minutes left to very warm applause. He was sitting on the bench when he heard his name surprisingly announced as the man of the match. If this was an attempt to encourage the striker, it seemed a bit cringingly overboard.

Hogh was also on the bench when Celtic were awarded a penalty after 75 minutes so couldn’t grab the ball in an effort to put everything to bed. Nygren accepted the responsibility instead and saw Nico Mantl make a brilliant diving block to keep Kilmarnock in the game.

The fans certainly appreciated Hogh’s endeavours and clearly believe that while the statistics books might state otherwise, he has already morally broken his Parkhead duck.

His neat finish was cruelly chalked off - after the Dane had completed the understandably comprehensive celebration routine - for a foul by Mika Baur in the build-up that very few saw. Referee John Beaton nevertheless seemed very sure having been called to his monitor and spent little time deliberating.

A clearly agitated Hogh then wasted a good chance to score shortly afterwards although credit should go to Mantl, the true man of the match, for blocking with his foot when the striker had just the keeper to beat. Mantl's later penalty stop - after a VAR check confirmed a handball by Aaron Tshibola had taken place inside the box – meant bottom-of-the-table Kilmarnock were still fighting until the end.

They came so close to taking the point their efforts certainly deserved. With the clock having ticked into the four minutes of additional time, substitute Eric Ring reached the byline and swung in a cross that Ieuan Owen somehow failed to connect with in the middle.

As for Celtic, with their No. 9 seemingly so out of touch and luck, their No. 5 stepped in. Scales scored the kind of goal that is eluding Hogh at present after he got on the end of Duran’s floated cross. The ball kissed the crossbar before landing in the net. That’s three goals for the defender this season – equal with Hogh.

A planned period of silence to commemorate the war dead was cut short before kick-off due to the volume of booing in the stadium. Beaton barely gave it ten seconds before blowing his whistle. It all felt a little unsettling with Celtic taking longest to get themselves focused, at the risk of very nearly conceding the first goal. As was the case at the death, the visitors came close to scoring right at the start. Tom Lowery even had two bites at the cherry, with Celtic goalkeeper Sam Johnstone the equal to his efforts both times.

Celtic sought to take advantage of the let-off and immediately got on with the seeming job in hand: helping Hogh get off the mark at Parkhead. Nygren tried to place a cross on his head after eight minutes but the striker was crowded out. It was almost as if the team had been specifically set up to let Hogh score. And he did. 4.13pm, the moment Celtic Park had been waiting for – or so it seemed.

With Jota, making his first start since April 2025, and Camilo Duran either side of Hogh and Nygren in the space behind, it ought to have been a centre-forward’s dream. Especially given all these players seemingly had one aim in mind: feed the Hogh.

Parkhead exploded with joy unconfined. Duran slipped the ball through to Nygren, who swivelled and played in Hogh. The Dane could not miss and to be fair, he didn’t. A very composed finish into the corner had him pointing to the heavens and crossing himself and making all manner of gestures of gratitude before VAR delivered the mother of all smackdowns: Goal disallowed.

Celtic secured the three points in the end, albeit with one or two scares. They have reached the latest international break in marginally better shape than last time, when successive Rangers defeats meant Martin O’Neill’s job seemed in very real jeopardy.

#1981. Wily veterans and the fountain of youth: The five key battles in Milan vs. Ferencvaros

AC Milan return to Europa League action at San Siro this evening for a must-win game against high-flyers Ferencvaros.

Starting their European campaign with two defeats (vs. Benfica and Bournemouth) and one win last left Milan down in 24th in the table, meaning that they need to turn things around if they are to mount a surge towards the top eight spots.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Tonight’s game will be far from straightforward though, as Ferencvaros have taken nine points from nine and therefore sit fourth in the table. They are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and are two points from the summit in their domestic league, with a game in hand to play.

Reports are suggesting that Ruben Amorim will turn to a youthful line-up for this one despite the status of being a must-win game. However, the spine of the team will still be made up of players who must deliver.

Starting with a rather unconventional battle, the one between the two goalkeepers Lorenzo Torriani and Dénes Dibusz could be potentially decisive, for obvious reasons. Ferencvaros have conceded just three goals in their three Europa games so far and just 10 in 10 in the league, and the 35-year-old veteran Dibusz has been a big part of that, even if there has been some rotation.

For Torriani, this is arguably his biggest opportunity in a Milan shirt. His only other start came in a Coppa Italia rout of Sassuolo, while he came off the bench in a Champions League defeat to Liverpool, and in the Bournemouth defeat. This is a huge chance for the 20-year-old to not only show he is a capable deputy in the present, but a potential Mike Maignan successor down the line.

There will also be two crucial duels involving the two Nagys, Oliver and Adam. The former will play at right-back and faces the difficult task of keeping Alphadjo Cisse quiet. The Italian is the Rossoneri’s top scorer this season and will be champing at the bit to build on his hat-trick against RB Salzburg. Oliver Nagy is dangerous going forward though, with two assists in his five starts, so Cisse will have to help out defensively too.

Adam Nagy meanwhile faces the task of stopping Milan’s second-top scorer, Adrien Rabiot. The Frenchman netted his fifth of the season in the derby against Inter, and Amorim has chosen to rely on his experience against an opponent who is also 31 years of age. The Hungarian signed from Spezia in the summer and is best known for his appearances at the 2016, 2020 and 2024 UEFA European Championships for his national team.

Ferencvaros have two main threats that Milan must keep quiet, especially the way that this game could play out with the visitors no doubt keen to contain and counter. Bamidele Yusuf is the first, and the Nigerian is expected to start up front this evening though he can also play and drift wide. He has six goals and three assists in 10 starts this season for the green and whites.

Bamidele Yusuf 🎯#UEL | @Fradi_HU pic.twitter.com/AXnt4XPaSu

— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) October 29, 2026

Sanhoun Diawara will have to do his bit to keep Yusuf quiet, but our feeling is that Koni De Winter will take on the man-marking duties just like he did with Inter’s lone striker Marcus Thuram in the derby. The Belgian has been undroppable in a literal sense, so we hope that no signs of fatigue are seen especially in transition, like against Bologna.

The visitors’ other danger man is Kristoffer Zachariassen, who matches Yusuf on nine goal contributions (seven goals, two assists) for the season. The 32-year-old Norwegian has plenty of experience and an eye for goal from the attacking midfield role, though his heat maps show he tends to drift to the right too.

So, it will be down to Ardon Jashari to keep tabs on him. Amorim and Milan are still waiting for the Swiss to put together a good run of solid starts after his arrival from Club Brugge for over €30m, and this is the kind of game that he needs to seize control of and dominate to show he is capable of being the anchor man, especially with Luka Modric’s retirement surely not far away.

#1980. Rockettes put 10 past Portchester – the match in pictures

The result leaves them second in the table with four wins and a draw from their opening five matches.

Bec Bell-Thorns set up two attacks early on with her runs and crosses from the right. First Kate Delilis diverted a chance over the bar and then a similar move soon after saw Millie Carter shoot high and wide just 3 minutes in. Aimee Hall-Guy did well in the Bognor area following a cross from the right but diverted wide from close range.

Bognor took the lead on 12 minutes when a corner fell to Sophia Poling who nodded it in despite a defender's efforts on the line. The Rockettes extended their lead on 15 minutes as Kate Delillis fired it in off a defender following Lucie Wright's freekick cross. Sophie Humphrey also hit the left post after a short run as Bognor dominated the opening 20 minutes.

Nicole Robinson saved comfortably from Hall-Guy's strike from outside the area. Lily West put a neat through ball to Char Heanen but her powerful strike was pushed over confidently by Robinson on 26 minutes. Lucie Selvester did well to cross the ball into the area to find Sophie Humphrey but after twisting and turning she brought out a good save by Sofie Harris.

Elena Butcher clipped the crossbar with her cross moments later for the visitors. On 33 minutes Poling hit a long range freekick directly high and wide as Bognor maintained their lead. Bognor went three goals up in the 35th minute. The visitors failed to clear their lines from Wright's corner before the ball fell to Humphrey who blasted it high into the roof of the net.

Bognor got their fourth goal on 40 minutes. A fine pass out wide onto the left found Lucie Wright in space and shen ran onto it before firing it over the goalkeeper and into the net. It got better for the hosts as Humphrey netted her second of the afternoon, following up the rebound from a previous strike on 44 minutes. HT 5-0.

After half time Niamh Andersson replaced Bell-Thorns.

Humphrey turned in the area quickly and forced a save over the bar from Harris. Humphrey studded in from close range for Bognor's 6th goal of the afternoon. It was scrappy in defence for the visitors who failed to clear the danger on 48 minutes. On 56 minutes Alice Gue was replaced by Ellie Jefkins.

Bognor made it seven on 58 minutes when Humphrey netted her fourth of the day following a low cross. Delillis set up Freya Boxer but after a nice run she hit the side netting with her strike. Bognor made another change on 62 minutes as Wright came off for Clara Castanheira.

Elena Williams hit a free-kick directly into Robinson's arms in a rare chance for the visitors. Carter's corner kick on the right bounced back out for a goal kick off the frame of goal moments later. Bognor got their 8th in the 66th minute as Humphrey closed down the ball before passing it square to Boxer in the box and she made no mistake, netting it along the deck and in.

Bognor got their ninth on 69 minutes. Andersson placed it nicely beyond defence for Delillis who fired it past the goalkeeper. On 70 minutes Talliah Anderson replaced Sophie Humphrey. Good work from Carter saw her pass back to Castanheira who curled it into the middle where Andersson was waiting but she diverted it wide of goal.

A cross from the left by Castanheira found Boxer in the box and she fired it high and in for Bognor's tenth goal on 76 minutes. A high corner bounced off Elena Williams and into the net for the visitors first goal of the afternoon as a consolation. The visitors also hit the post moments later as the goal perked up the opposition in for the first time in the second half.

Gue came back on for Macie Downs on 86 minutes in a rolling substitution. But despite more chances for Boxer for the Rockettes towards the end it was a comprehensive victory for the Bognor women's side.

They travel to Andover New Street on Sunday, November 15, at 2pm before playing at home on Sunday 22 against AFC Varsity with kick off at 2pm.

#1979. Liam Scales' honest Celtic form verdict after avoiding 'nightmare' vs Kilmarnock

It wasn't pretty and it wasn't memorable, but as is usually the case under Martin O'Neill, Celtic got the job done.

The manager couldn't have picked a kinder fixture – at home against the side bottom of the table – for his team to return to winning ways in the Premiership. Yet Celtic made hard work of beating Kilmarnock.

Sam Johnstone produced a crucial double save inside the opening minute to deny Tom Lowery and if Ieuan Owen had connected cleanly with Erik Ring's cross in stoppage time, Celtic would be back in crisis mode. Alas, the hosts held on.

Liam Scales' first-half finish proved decisive on an afternoon permeated with missed chances for both sides.

The slender victory restored Celtic's four-point lead at the Premiership summit going into the international break, although Rangers have a game in hand.

They took care of Besiktas midweek, but O'Neill's reigning champions hadn't won in the league in a fortnight, losing to Falkirk and drawing with Dundee United, underlining the significance of Sunday's win.

"It was definitely important," Scales said. "Two games [in the league] without a win is bad enough, but three would have been a nightmare.

"We knew we needed that win and can go into the break and refresh. Some of the lads can rest and recover and hopefully we’ll come back in this form.

"I do think confidence is a massive part of our group and it was probably hit a little bit. The win against a top side like Besiktas has boosted us a little bit. There’s kind of a better mood around. We just want to keep adding good results."

Celtic's Liam Scales celebrates with his team-mates. (Image: Steve Welsh/PA)

Celtic entered the last international break following three consecutive losses to Rangers, Ferencvaros and Rangers again.

Things felt ominous, with O'Neill publicly considering his future after the second of those derby defeats.

But Celtic rallied and defeated Motherwell in their first game back. Things weren't smooth over the following eight matches, but as players return from injury, Scales feels positive about the future.

"We had Yang back on Sunday, Jota is obviously starting. These guys are getting back to full sharpness and getting minutes," he said. "Hopefully this will help and we can build on it.

"We know we haven’t been good enough between the last international window and this one. We’ve let a few results go and we’re not exactly where we want to be.

"It was just really important to win these last two games before the break and be in a good place for coming back."

Celtic leading the league was rare last season. Only in the dying minutes of the campaign did they return to the Premiership summit after Hearts knocked them off their perch back in September 2025.

"We always want to be on top of the table. We don’t want to be chasing," Scales stated. "We want to be a good arm’s length from the challengers.

"That is the goal all season – to stay top. It’s important to us but obviously there are so many games to play. You go through really busy spells and both teams will be challenged. But we are just happy where we are now.

"It hasn’t been spoken about – but it doesn’t need to be spoken about. We all know the standards at this club that have been set over a number of years.

"It doesn’t need to be discussed where we want to be – because it’s top of the table. Last season wasn’t what we wanted at all and we don’t want a repeat of that."

Scales scored his second goal in four games against Kilmarnock, connecting sweetly with Camilo Duran's looped cross.

The Irishman's effort sailed over opposition goalkeeper Nico Mantl and into the back of the net to break the deadlock in the 26th minute.

"It took an age to come down," Scales reflected. "I wasn’t sure if it was going to land on the roof of the net. I was just trying to guide it on target and luckily enough it went in.

"I don’t really have a target for goals – it’s more about clean sheets for me. But it’s nice. We’ve done a lot of work on set pieces, we’re getting the ball into the box more rather than going short and I suppose you always get a bit excited as a centre half when you go forward for a corner.

"It is nice to score and hopefully I can get a few more between now and the end of the season. I felt we should have killed the game in the second half. We were unlucky not to score.

"When you are only a goal up the atmosphere can get a bit nervy and that can translate onto the pitch. But I don’t think we were troubled too much. It was comfortable but it would have looked better if we’d scored some more."

For goals this season, Scales is now level with Kasper Hogh. The striker thought he'd ended his 16-game scoring drought on Sunday, only for VAR to intervene and disallow the strike for a foul in the build-up by Mika Baur.

Hogh didn't let his frustrations boil over, instead working even harder and offering a useful focal point in attack.

He earned the in-stadium man of the match award and was deservedly applauded off the field in the 71st minute. Scales is certain the goals will come, even if he snatched one from Hogh against Kilmarnock.

"He’s been brilliant. He keeps doing the right things and eventually it will fall for him," the defender added. "He was so unlucky with his goal being ruled out.

"And he told me he was right behind me with the goal I scored! If I’d known that I might have left it!

"It will fall for him. He’s a goal scorer and a good player. His all-round game was brilliant, he held the ball up really well. He’s just been unlucky. But his attitude has been brilliant.

"If he keeps doing the right things it will work out for him. He has an amazing attitude and that’s why I really believe he will be successful."

#1978. 'Provoked' - Brentford's Keith Andrews makes Chema Andres claim after Igor Thiago red card at Brighton

Brentford boss Keith Andrews questioned the use of VAR in the Premier League after Igor Thiago’s first-half dismissal proved costly in a 2-0 defeat at high-flying Brighton.

Bees striker Thiago was initially shown a yellow card by referee Michael Oliver after reacting to a shirt pull and subsequent push from Albion midfielder Chema Andres, who was also booked.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But the punishment was upgraded to red on review as match official Oliver deemed the Brazil international used “force” to push his opponent in the face with a raised arm.

Brentford’s only other league defeat this term came after Yehor Yarmoliuk was shown a first-half red card in last month’s 2-1 home loss to Liverpool.

Andrews accepted his players must take responsibility for their conduct but questioned the circumstances surrounding both incidents.

“We’ve lost two games in the league this season and both have been when we’ve gone down to 10 men, so you need to analyse yourself first clearly,” he said.

“On both scenarios, we can do better. On both scenarios, the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation and antagonise our player and react towards our player in an aggressive way.

“Players’ reactions now mean everything. I’m going to reiterate it: we should do better. But the game is in a state now of a place I don’t particularly like. We’ll have to have a look at that because it’s costing us.”

Brentford were already trailing at the time of Thiago’s sending-off following a stunning long-range opener from Brighton midfielder Diego Gomez.

Disgruntled away fans chanted “2-0 to the referee” and “Michael Oliver, it’s all about you” after Pascal Gross doubled Albion’s lead with a 42nd-minute penalty awarded for Keane Lewis-Potter’s shirt pull on Luka Vuskovic.

Andrews, who felt his side should have been “cuter” in the penalty incident, was frustrated Oliver was sent to the pitch-side monitor before changing his initial decision on Thiago.

“I’m struggling to believe in this day and age where we see the referee’s call on pitch and the bar of where they’re given the licence to referee in-game, which is what I should think it should be, but he’s been sent to the screen,” he said.

“We play on the edge, we’re a team that likes to play on the edge, I want us to be on the edge. But it clearly cost us.”

Brighton climbed to second after marking their return to the Amex Stadium following five successive away matches with a comfortable victory.

Gomez lashed into the top-left corner with his left foot to follow up his goal from the halfway line in last month’s 5-0 thrashing of rivals Crystal Palace.

Seagulls head coach Fabian Hurzeler said: “It’s a funny story because yesterday he trained shooting with the left foot and I couldn’t see him scoring today with this left foot – the shots weren’t great.

“I asked him after the game where he got this quality from overnight. It’s a huge improvement in a very short period.”

Albion’s win was a seventh from 10 top-flight games and lifted them above Manchester City and back to within five points of leaders Arsenal.

Asked when Seagulls supporters can start getting really excited, Hurzeler said: “They should be always excited if they watch our game, and that’s our job to make them excited.

“I always say they can dream, they can have high expectations on us, but these are things we can’t control.”

#1975. 'At fault' .. 'quite sloppy' .. 'very few touches' - ratings from Crawley Town's embarrassing loss to Wimborne Town

Seung-Woo Yang gave Wimborne the lead with a magical finish ten minutes into the game.

Crawley dominated possession but failed to test the Wimborne keeper, with a lack of creativity and attacking impetus letting them down.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The Reds looked to be building some momentum early in the second half but that soon faded.

With ten minutes remaining Cam Munn tapped it home to make it 2-0 – the win putting the Magpies into the second round and giving the Wimborne a day they will never forget and Crawley one they will want to in a hurry.

Here are our player ratings – and the fact the man we picked out as Crawley’s best operator wasn’t even on the pitch in the first half says it all…

Vito Mannone: 3.5 – The experienced goalkeeper was at fault for Wimborne’s opener in the first half as his throw fell short of its target and the home side capitalised. Did produce a good save while Wimborne led 2-0.

Kellan Gordon: 3 – Drove down the right hand side well at times and got into good crossing positions but his deliveries failed to beat the first man on a number of occasions or were too close to the keeper.

Charlie Barker: 4 – The 23 year old was in midfield once again and battled well at times winning some of his aerial duels but was quite sloppy on the ball throughout the game.

Priestley Farquharson: 5 – One of the Reds’ stronger players in what was an embarrassing performance. Won most of his duels and used his strength and physicality well during the first half. He had to come off with an injury midway through the second 45.

Danilo Orsi: 3 – Crawley opted to play direct particularly in the first half and the striker struggled to make any impact at all having very few touches before being taken off at half time.

Stephen Duke-McKenna: 4 – Had very little joy down the right hand side and rarely got the rub of the green with the solidity of the Wimborne backline.

Lewis Richards: 3.5 – Quiet first half from the left back. Didn’t offer anything from an attacking front to drive Crawley forward let alone defensively.

Jonny Russell: 4.5 – The Irishman was a left centre-back again and definitely improved in the second half with some good runs from deep.

Jude Arthurs: 4 – Former Bromley midfielder struggled to galvanise his teammates as Crawley captain and wasn’t really involved in the build-up as the Reds looked to play it long, struggling to play through the 7th tier side.

Dylan Morgan: 5 – Just like Duke-McKenna, didn’t have a lot of luck down his flank on the left. Had a few shots fired wide and his crosses did not lead to anything prosperous.

Kai Jennings: 3 – The Wimbledon loanee had a tough time in midfield but did have a good effort in the first half while it was 1-0 which flashed wide.

Josh Flint: 6 – Gave the Reds some momentum when he came on at half-time, driving his team up the pitch with his marauding runs and was by far Crawley’s best player.

Nathan Tinsdale: 4 – The youngster struggled in difficult circumstances like many of his teammates.

Pemi Aderoju: 4 – Was more effective up front than Orsi, winning flick ons from the lofted balls up front. Had one great chance five minutes into the second half which he volleyed straight at the keeper.

Ben Heneghan: 3.5 – The 6ft 3 centre back came on to make his debut but failed to make any sort of impact.

Malcolm Ebiowei: 5 – A few neat touches and dribbles from Derby County attacker but didn’t have enough time to effect the game.

#1973. Celtic star’s agonising goal drought inspires ruthless online game

Kasper Hogh’s struggles in front of goal have now inspired an online game where the aim is simple: try to make the Celtic striker score.

The only problem is it appears almost impossible.

Hogh is enduring a torrid dry spell for the Hoops, having failed to find the net in his last 15 appearances. It has now been 1,053 minutes since the £11 million striker last scored, against Kilmarnock back in August.

And someone has decided to make light of his misfortune by creating Hogh’s Hotshots: The Impossible Finisher.

Players take control of Hogh and attempt to fire the ball beyond the goalkeeper, only for an increasingly ridiculous selection of obstacles to get in the way.

Efforts can be saved by the goalkeeper, crash back off the woodwork, or fly harmlessly into row Z. At one stage, Hogh simply falls over while attempting to shoot. Even finding the back of the net does not necessarily guarantee success, with VAR capable of intervening to chalk the goal off.

The Celtic VAR denial you can't 'unsee' as leading ref drops unflinching take

3-man panel split over Celtic VAR flashpoint as key ref claim made

Watch Ex-SPFL boss see red after astonishing rammy with former Premiership star

Things have hardly been going Hogh’s way recently, although the timing of the game is perhaps unfortunate given his improved display against Kilmarnock on Sunday.

Hogh earned Celtic’s Man of the Match award after producing one of his more encouraging performances in recent weeks, impressing with his hold-up and link-up play.

The striker even thought he had finally ended his agonising wait for a goal with a well-taken finish at Celtic Park. His celebrations were cut short, however, when VAR intervened, and the goal was disallowed because of a foul in the build-up.

The drought therefore continues, but Sunday provided genuine encouragement that Hogh could finally be edging closer to ending it.

After 15 games without a goal, Celtic will hope the real-life Hogh proves a lot easier to get scoring than his virtual counterpart.

#1972. Everything we’ve done in training was for nothing – Blackwell embarrassed at Crawley Town’s Cup loss at Wimborne

The Reds slipped to a new low as they were outplayed by seventh tier Wimborne Town, who beat them 2-0 in the FA Cup first round – and it was the second straight season Cralwey had gone out at this stage to a non-league side.

Goals from Seung-woo Yang and Cameron Munn secured the deserved win for the hosts, as Crawley were played off the park.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Speaking with club media after the game, interim manager Blackwell said he was ‘embarrassed’. He added: “I’m not very happy with what I’ve seen today, and I’ve learnt a lot today. This was a key game for me because expectation was on the players. I wanted to see how they would react with expectations. And I’m sorry to say I’ve not been impressed with what I’ve seen today.”

The Reds came into this game after good results against Tranmere and Oldham – and were long favourites to proceed to the next round.

Crawley fans travelled in their numbers but left disappointed and deeply unhappy at the performance. Blackwell said “I’ve got to apologise to the Crawley fans. And there were some here and there’s some not very happy fans. And quite right, I wouldn’t be happy.

“This has been a really interesting two weeks since I’ve been here. And what I’m concerned about is the undulation in the performances. That, for me, isn’t good. I’ve told everybody where the club is. They know where it is. And while I’m here, I’ll work my socks off for the club. That’s what I’ll do.

“But the players have got to have a long hard look at themselves. They’ve got to decide whether they want to be playing at clubs like this next year or in the Football League. It’s a simple equation. They’ve got to know and have that desire for me to be professional footballers and want to be in the Football League. It’s as simple as that. It’s not hard to work that out.”

Blackwell had mentioned in his pre-match preview about paying the utmost respect to the opposition, but he didn’t feel they did. When asked about that, he said “No I didn’t. I said to the players if I started, I’d still be there at 10 o’clock tonight. All the things that we’ve tried to do and everything we’ve done in training; everything was for nothing.

“If you can’t follow the plans and you can’t follow the roles and responsibilities and you duck out of physical challenges… they were a team that were physical, we knew that. We didn’t need to fight them. We just needed to play some football. We didn’t do any of it. So, I’m bitterly disappointed with what I’ve seen.”

Crawley’s next fixture is against Brentford U21s in the Jersey Mikes’ Trophy on Tuesday (Nov 10) then nothing until Saturday, November 21, when they take on Fleetwood Town at home, which gives Blackwell some time to get the side’s confidence back up.

He said “We saw a good performance against Tranmere and could have won it. We went to Oldham and won it. Then I see this today. So, I don’t know what I’m going to get in the next game.

“And as a manager or as a coach, it’s a nightmare when you don’t know what the performance level your team’s going to give you. I need consistency in performances. We need consistency as a club. That isn’t consistent, so I’ve got to work out what we can do with it.”

#1971. John McGinn stars in eight-goal thriller as EPL record broken while Scott McTominay rescued by bizarre goal

Scotland international John McGinn warmed up for this week’s Nations League fixtures by playing a major role in Aston Villa’s thrilling 4-4 draw with Manchester United on Sunday afternoon, but left fuming after two dramatic late goals denied them a vital win.

McGinn, 31, helped his side get off to a perfect start at Old Trafford, assisting Alysson's opening goal in the first minute, before Nicolas Jackson added a second just three minutes later. A penalty from Bruno Fernandes (16) and a Youri Tielemans strike (44) levelled the scores before half-time, though.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, the away side took the lead once again just three minutes after the restart when McGinn buried his penalty beyond Senne Lammens, and it looked like Villa had sealed the win when Leon Goretzka scored his first goal for the club in the 53rd minute. Dramatically, though, Manchester United somehow stole a point with two injury-time strikes from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu.

Having been just seconds away from breaking a run of three games without a win, McGinn was left hugely frustrated as he lamented Villa’s late collapse. “We have to manage these moments better,” McGinn told Match of the Day. “Not a lot of teams will come here 2-0 and give goals away. We have to defend better in those positions. In the last 10 minutes of each half, we have to manage better.

“We have a lot of inexperienced players but a lot of talent, and that's why we score goals. It doesn't matter if United are low on confidence; you're always up against it. We lost two points. We threw it away. The last five minutes were just madness. It's going to sting. The manager is a winner; he'll be hurting the way we are. We go play international football but he'll dwell on it for two weeks.”

The thrilling draw means McGinn’s side are winless since their 2-1 triumph over Manchester City on October 24, leaving them in 10th place in the English Premier League. Meanwhile, their hosts are now the only side in the league to have won just one game this season, leaving them in 18th place and amongst the relegation spots as pressure mounts on head coach Michael Carrick.

However, United did set a little piece of history during the chaotic 4-4 draw with Unai Emery’s side, as they became the first team in English Premier League history to trail by two goals on two separate occasions within a single match and successfully fight back to level the score both times.

Elsewhere, McGinn’s international teammate Scott McTominay saw his Napoli side rescue a point against top of the table Lazio at the Diego Armando Maradona Stadium thanks to an own goal in the second half. The Partenopei currently occupy 10th place in the Serie A after losing four of their opening 11 games, and looked set to fall to a fifth defeat when their unbeaten visitors took the lead through Davide Fratessi after 28 minutes.

Napoli took a share of the spoils though in strange circumstances when substitute Alfonso Pedraza smashed beyond his own goalkeeper while under pressure from McTominay just three minutes after being introduced as a half-time substitute. Already 14 points behind the league leaders, pressure is mounting on head coach Massimiliano Allegri, but remained defiant after the stalemate.

“Let us remember we are not out of Serie A, the Coppa Italia or the Champions League yet," said Allegri. “There are difficult moments over the course of a campaign. I believe we need to deal with them in a spirit of calm. When we are in the middle of the storm, we manage to get the boat to shore somehow.

#1970. Rangers 'flying swan' penalty blasted by two top refs as third backs VAR

James Penrice has been compared to a swan flying through the air as three former top referees ran the rule over Rangers’ controversial penalty against St Mirren.

Nick Walsh pointed to the spot after the Light Blues defender went down under a challenge from Samuel Ramos, with VAR allowing the on-field decision to stand.

But the call has split the refereeing experts, with Mark Clattenburg and Bobby Madden unconvinced there was enough in the challenge to warrant a spot-kick, while Dermot Gallagher stressed how difficult it would have been for VAR to overturn Walsh’s decision.

Clattenburg, speaking on the So Near, Yet So VAR podcast, said: “Sometimes the best decisions are the ones you don’t give.

Read more: Celtic star’s agonising goal drought inspires ruthless online game

“What doesn’t help Nick Walsh is the way the Rangers player goes down. It isn’t consistent with the contact.

“When you start seeing the small contact on the foot, there is contact, there is no doubt. But when that contact makes him fly through the air like a swan, then you’ve got to question if there was enough contact to award a penalty kick.

“I don’t believe there is. Again, the best decision is the one you don’t give, so just play on.

“Football is a contact sport. Not every bit of contact is a foul, we have to accept that.

“Penrice’s actions aren’t consistent with the contact on the foot. That is enough for a referee to say, ‘I’ve got a doubt’, and just play on.”

Madden was in agreement with his So Near, Yet So VAR co-host and reckoned Walsh had become too focused on the contact itself.

He said: “I don’t think it is enough contact.

“If you look at it from the referee’s perspective, he is very well placed and he will see Penrice take the touch away from goal.

“He will then see the defender coming in and trying to play the ball, not playing the ball and making contact.

“Again, hyper-focused on this contact, probably not recognising that the reaction from Penrice did not merit the contact he received, and he has awarded a penalty kick very confidently.

“It is very difficult for VAR to intervene because they will look at it and see this contact.

“That’s not enough for a penalty kick. It’s not enough for that reaction and not enough for a penalty kick.”

Former Premier League referee Gallagher offered a different perspective when the incident came under the microscope on Sky Sports’ Ref Watch.

He said: “He couldn’t have a better view than the referee and, what you said, the defender definitely doesn’t get the ball.

“But where the referee is, he’s got the perfect view. There’s the ball, Rangers player plays the ball, he doesn’t.

“It’s very, very hard to go against a referee in that situation, if at all possible. And there’s the touch there.”

MARK CLATTENBURG: NO PENALTY Accepted there was contact but felt it was not enough to justify Penrice’s “fly through the air like a swan” reaction, believing Walsh should have played on.

BOBBY MADDEN: NO PENALTY Felt Walsh became “hyper-focused” on the contact without considering whether Penrice’s reaction matched it, insisting there was not enough in the challenge for a spot-kick.

DERMOT GALLAGHER: VAR RIGHT TO STICK WITH CALL Pointed to Walsh having the “perfect view”, Ramos failing to win the ball and there being contact on Penrice, making it “very, very hard” for VAR to overturn the on-field decision.

Overall: Two against the penalty, with Gallagher backing VAR’s decision not to intervene.

#1969. Steve Herbert: Just when we thought it couldn't get any worse, Crawley Town hit a new low

The most embarrassing performance and result since we became a football league club in 2011.

As a football club we have hit a new low, when we already thought sitting bottom of the entire football league couldn’t get any worse, we end up being out fought and outplayed by a team who plays at the same level as Three Bridges.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Let that sink in for a minute… a team who plays in a stadium not much different to Jubilee Field has just knocked us out of the FA Cup first round in front of a national television audience.

Losing last season at Boreham Wood at the same stage was bad, but this is next level stuff.

Only this club could produce a result like this one. Four hundred and seventy six Reds fans gave up a whole Remembrance Sunday to attend this horror show in Dorset. Wimborne is probably one of the trickiest places to get too, especially by public transport. It’s quicker to get to Manchester and Liverpool by train than it is to get to the South West. Yet we take the largest away following of the season, and the players let us down like that. Absolutely disgusting.

After talking up all the positivity of the last two league results against Tranmere & Oldham, it’s such a shame that the team have let Kevin Blackwell down so spectacularly. All I can say is thank god the Rotherham game has been postponed. At least it saves us another wasteful day out.

Where do we go from here? Who knows. All I know is if I was one of those players who have let the club down massively and embarrassed every fan who attended and those that watched at home, then a reaction needs to be seen at home to Fleetwood Town in the shape of a performance and a win.

#1967. Scotland international celebrates Pocognoli call-up with rare assist but is left to rue 52 second mistake

Scotland international Ryan Porteous celebrated his recall to the national team by grabbing a rare assist for LAFC, but was left to rue an early mistake as his side fell to a 2-1 away defeat against Seattle Sounders on Sunday night.

Porteous, 27, was named in the Scotland squad by head coach Sebastien Pocognoli as an injury replacement for Stephen Welsh at the weekend, with the Swansea City defender ruled out after picking up an injury in the 3-1 EFL Championship defeat to Portsmouth last Tuesday.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It means Porteous could make his first Scotland appearance since he was introduced as a late substitute in the 1-0 Nations League play-off win in Greece back in March 2025, as the national team prepares for a double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland later this week.

The former Hibs centre-back added to his successful week by picking up his first assist of the season for Los Angeles FC as they fell to a narrow defeat at Seattle in their last regular season game. However, the clash began in disastrous fashion for the visitors, with Slovakian international Albert Rusnak putting Seattle into the lead after just 52 seconds at Lumen Field.

With Los Angeles in possession of the ball from kick-off, Hugo Lloris’ attempt to pass the ball back to Porteous caused confusion, with the Scottish defender and Mathieu Choiniere appearing to get in each other’s way. The latter lost the ball under pressure, allowing Cristian Roldan to pinch the ball and cross for Rusnak to tap into an empty net to put the home side into an early lead.

The home side then added a second just after the half-hour mark through winger Sebastian Gomez, with the 20-year-old’s shot from just inside the area deflecting into the top corner beyond Lloris to put the hosts into a commanding first-half lead as they looked to get a win that would seal their place in the end-of-season MLS playoffs, which begins later this month.

LAFC did their best to launch a comeback, with the visitors having 13 attempts on goal in the second 45 to Seattle’s zero. However, they couldn’t to find a breakthrough until the 82nd minute, with Porteous rising highest to Leo Walta’s free-kick, and heading across goal for centre-back partner Eddie Segura to bullet home and reduce the deficit.

In the end, though, the second-half onslaught was not enough to rescue a point in the Emerald City, as LAFC ended the regular Western Conference season in sixth place on 47 points, with 12 wins, 11 draws and 11 defeats, setting up a round of 16 clash with St. Louis City in the MLS playoffs on November 23.

“Conceding a goal inside the first minute completely changes the game plan,” lamented LAFC defender Segura. “We can't keep putting ourselves in a position where we are chasing matches from the opening whistle. It is a bad habit we have to fix immediately before the playoffs start.”

#1966. Little Common hold heads high despite defeat to Roffey

Having suffered a heavy 8-0 defeat against the same opposition on the opening weekend of the season, Common showed just how far they have progressed with a resolute display that kept them firmly in contention throughout.

The visitors enjoyed the lion’s share of possession during the opening period, but Common remained organised and difficult to break down, restricting Roffey's opportunities despite their territorial advantage. When the visitors did find a way through, goalkeeper Matt Cruttwell was in fine form, producing two smart saves to keep the scores level.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

However, Common's resistance was finally broken on the stroke of half-time when a neat passing move from the visitors allowed Roffey to take a slender advantage into the interval.

The second half followed a similar pattern, with Roffey enjoying plenty of possession but finding clear-cut chances difficult to come by against a hardworking Common side.

Cruttwell was again called into action, producing an excellent save low to his left to prevent the visitors from doubling their advantage.

Despite spending long periods without the ball, Common continued to battle for every challenge and remained within touching distance of an equaliser as the contest entered its closing stages.

The home side's best opportunity arrived late on when Sam Ellis rose to meet a delivery into the area, but his header flashed across the face of goal and away to safety. It proved to be Common's final opportunity as Roffey held on to secure all three points.

Boss Russ Eldridge said: “I thought the lads put in a really disciplined and hard-working performance against a very good Roffey side. They are up near the top of the table for a reason and we knew we would have to work extremely hard without the ball.

“When you consider we lost 8-0 to them on the opening day of the season, I think today's performance shows how far we have come. We were organised, difficult to break down and, despite them having plenty of possession, I didn't feel they created too many clear-cut opportunities.

“It was disappointing to concede right on half-time because we had worked so hard to keep them out. We stayed in the game throughout the second half and always felt we might nick something.

“The effort and commitment from the players couldn't be questioned. We now need to build on these performances and start turning them into points. If we continue showing that level of determination and togetherness, I'm confident results will come.”

#1965. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.
